summary: On paper this one is close: Houston's best edge is to hold up vs four (Houston ranks 3rd in QB hit + sack rate vs 4 or fewer rushers, 11%), while Washington's best counter is to hunt explosives (Washington ranks 13th in explosive play rate, 9.0%). Under center, C.J. Stroud ranks 7th of 31 in EPA per dropback and Jayden Daniels ranks 16th; x-factor: Stefon Diggs catches 62% of his targets, 8.3 yards downfield on average, and his spot: short (0-9 yards) to the left (26% of targets). Houston's defense allows 76% completions there. The model favors Houston at 52%, mostly on passing matchup (1.6 pts) and starting QB (1.3 pts).

HOU.detail: Houston ranks 3rd in QB hit + sack rate vs 4 or fewer rushers (11%). Washington's defense ranks 31st (13% generated).
Houston ranks 27th in broken tackles per touch (4.3%). Washington's defense ranks 1st (10.2% missed).
Houston ranks 5th in early-down EPA per dropback (+0.18). Washington's defense ranks 14th (+0.08 allowed).

WAS.detail: Washington's defense ranks 24th in EPA per dropback vs blitz (+0.03 allowed). Houston ranks 2nd (+0.10).
Washington's defense ranks 23rd in EPA per dropback with motion (+0.04 allowed). Houston ranks 3rd (+0.10).
Washington ranks 13th in explosive play rate (9.0%). Houston's defense ranks 25th (9.3% allowed).
